metadata.title: An odd-period product for focal inversions of outer billiard polygons
metadata.description: For a fixed odd least-period elliptic billiard family with a strictly nested nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic, we prove constancy of the product of the signed straight-edge areas obtained by unit inversion of the outer tangent-polygon vertices about the two original billiard foci. Every admissible coprime star turning number, the critical triangular case and fixed repeated traversals are included. This proves the assertion conjectured as k904,a in Reznik--Garcia--Koiller arXiv2004.12497v11, Table10 (earlier v10 label k808,a). The proof gives the explicit inverse-edge factorization, cancels double principal parts in the cyclic area sum, and applies the classical complementary zero/pole divisor argument on a compact torus. Stachel canonical coordinates, established Jacobi and cyclic elliptic identities, and earlier complex billiard and complementary-area techniques are credited. Original-vertex inverse areas and outer-locus-focus inversions are distinct targets. No exact earlier general proof was verified in two independent bounded priority audits; historical novelty remains undetermined. The final journal text of The talented Mr. Inversive Triangle was subscription-limited, open author versions were read, and selected-passage and unresolved-source limitations are preserved. No first-proof, absolute-priority, new general elliptic-method or current-worldwide-open claim is made. The deposit includes a concise research note and a portable source/verification archive preserving original submissions, exact controls, separately labeled numerical diagnostics and authored audit records. Finite checks support rather than replace the universal proof. AI tools were used extensively in solving, writing, computation, source investigation and independent internal adversarial checking. This is an unrefereed preprint without independent human peer review or formal proof-assistant verification.

abstract_and_description_contract.whole_original_abstract_tex: For a periodic billiard family between an ellipse and a strictly nested nondegenerate confocal elliptical caustic, form the outer polygon by intersecting consecutive tangents at the billiard vertices. Invert its vertices in the unit circles centered at the two original billiard foci, and join successive images by straight segments. We prove that the product of the resulting signed areas is constant for every odd least period, including primitive stars. This proves the invariant conjectured as k904,a in the pinned 2020 list of Reznik, Garcia and Koiller. An explicit inverse-edge factorization reduces the area to a cyclic elliptic sum. Its double principal parts cancel, leaving two simple poles and complementary half-period zeros. The triangular critical case and repeated traversals are included. The analytic methods are classical; no first-proof or absolute-priority claim is made. This AI-assisted research note is unrefereed.

source_claim_expectations_not_new_verdic.domain: Noncircular outer ellipse a>b>0, original foci f_±=(±c,0), c^2=a^2-b^2. Strictly nested nondegenerate confocal ELLIPTICAL caustic alpha>beta>0. Odd LEAST period N>=3; every admissible coprime star turning number included.
source_claim_expectations_not_new_verdic.outer_polygon: Q_j is the intersection of the tangents to the ORIGINAL billiard ellipse at consecutive billiard vertices P_j,P_{j+1}. The real intersections are finite; the manuscript puts each Q outside the original ellipse and original foci inside it.
source_claim_expectations_not_new_verdic.inversion: J_f(Q)=f+(Q-f)/||Q-f||^2 is unit-circle inversion about each ORIGINAL billiard focus. Invert vertices and join successive images by STRAIGHT segments. This is not whole-edge inversion into circular arcs.
source_claim_expectations_not_new_verdic.signed_area: B_±=1/2 sum_j det(J_{f_±}(Q_j),J_{f_±}(Q_{j+1})); ordered signed shoelace/algebraic area for stars, not union-of-faces area.
source_claim_expectations_not_new_verdic.full_main_claim: B_+ B_- is a POSITIVE constant along every stated odd least-period family. Both inversions are defined at every real outer vertex; reversal negates each signed area and leaves the product unchanged.
boundary_contract: All admissible coprime star windings; choose forward 0<tau<N/2 with gcd(tau,N)=1, with reversal handled separately.
The exceptional primitive triangular case N=3,tau=1 is included, not removed.
For any fixed r-fold traversal of an odd least-period orbit, each area scales by r and the product by r^2; total-list parity does not replace least-period scope.
No assertion for collapsed or hyperbolic caustics. No unrestricted even-least-period theorem is stated.
The outer locus may have its major-axis order reversed; do not assume A_o>B_o.
The original foci are generally NOT the outer locus's foci. Original-vertex product k903,a and outer-locus-focus inversion k906 are distinct targets.
The inverse-area-ratio conjecture k806,a is not assumed and is not automatically a follow-up.
circular_and_scale_contract: Circular case is a separate rigid-rotation calculation: R_o=a/cos(pi tau/N); each signed inverse area is N sin(2pi tau/N)/(2 R_o^2), and the product is its square.
Similarity by s>0 of the original configuration while retaining UNIT inversion scales the product by s^(-4).
Replacing both unit inversion radii by rho multiplies the product by rho^8.
proof_explanation_expectations: Stachel coordinates produce an explicit inverse-edge expression; focal squared distance factors as alpha^2/q^2 times (1+k sn u)(U+kV sn u), generally two distinct factors.
Complex squared norms are continued bilinearly without conjugation; do not confuse them with real Euclidean norms.
The source tracks double poles at r0±v and simple poles at r0±3v, including the triangular critical fiber. Cyclic cancellation removes double principal parts.
The cyclic area F on C/(L Z+4p Z), L=4K/N, has exactly two simple poles and two complementary half-period zeros; classical divisor/compactness reasoning makes F(u)F(u+L/2) constant.
Central reflection switches original-focus inversions; B_-(w)=B_+(w+2K), and odd N gives 2K congruent L/2 modulo L.
Real edge contributions are positive in the chosen forward orientation, supporting positivity rather than a merely possibly-zero product.
